title: Fried Kibbeh with Spiced Lamb Filling
summary: Crisp, deep-brown torpedoes of bulgur and lamb, filled with lamb, onion, warm spices and a touch of pomegranate molasses. Serve warm with lemon and mint.
equipment: deep frying pan or heavy pot

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Rinse the bulgur in a sieve, then cover with cold water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain and squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands; wet bulgur makes a sticky dough.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6-8 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the lamb, cinnamon, allspice, salt and pepper and cook for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and it reads 71 °C. Spoon off excess fat, stir in the pomegranate molasses and cool completely.

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Process the shell lamb, onion, spices, salt and pepper for about 1 minute, to a smooth paste. Keeping the meat cold helps it bind.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Add the bulgur and 1 ice cube and process for 1-2 minutes more, adding the second ice cube if it warms, until it forms a smooth, pliable dough with no visible grains. Chill for 30 minutes so it firms up.

steps.title: Hollow
steps.text: With wet hands, roll the dough into 16 balls (about 35 g each). Hold one in your palm and push a finger into it, turning and pressing to make a shell with walls about 5 mm thick.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Spoon in a heaped tablespoon of cold filling, pinch the opening closed and roll into a torpedo with pointed ends. Patch any cracks with wet fingers, then chill on a lined tray for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 4 cm oil to 180 °C. Fry 4-5 at a time for 5-6 minutes, turning, until deep brown and the shell reads 71 °C in its thickest part. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with lemon and mint.

tips: Keep a bowl of cold water beside you while shaping; wet hands stop the dough sticking and smooth the surface.
If the shells crack, the dough is too dry: process in a spoonful of cold water.
Thin, even walls are the goal; thick shells stay dense in the middle.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Fried kibbeh keep in the fridge for 3 days; reheat at 200 °C for 10 minutes, until piping hot (74 °C). Shaped, unfried kibbeh freeze for 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
